## Guided Tutorial 3.1: Reading the Charles River O2C Entity-Relationship Diagram

**Context and objective.** In this tutorial, you will study the O2C core ER diagram and practice identifying tables, keys, relationships, and cardinality. The goal is to develop fluency in reading ER diagrams so that you can navigate any table group you encounter in later chapters or in professional practice.

**Prerequisites.** You need the Charles River O2C ER diagram (@fig-03-07) and the crow's foot notation reference (@fig-03-04).

**Step-by-step instructions.**

**Step 1.** Locate @fig-03-07, the Charles River O2C core ER diagram. Begin by counting the tables shown. You should identify the core tables in the revenue path: Customer, SalesOrder, SalesOrderLine, Item, Shipment, ShipmentLine, SalesInvoice, SalesInvoiceLine, CashReceipt, and CashReceiptApplication. Each table is represented as a rectangle with a header bar and a list of columns. Notice that Item has a gray header, because it belongs to the Master Data group rather than to O2C.

**Step 2.** Identify the primary key of each table. Look for the column marked "PK" in each table. The primary keys include CustomerID (Customer), SalesOrderID (SalesOrder), SalesOrderLineID (SalesOrderLine), ItemID (Item), ShipmentID (Shipment), ShipmentLineID (ShipmentLine), SalesInvoiceID (SalesInvoice), SalesInvoiceLineID (SalesInvoiceLine), CashReceiptID (CashReceipt), and CashReceiptApplicationID (CashReceiptApplication). Notice that the Charles River database uses surrogate primary keys, single-column integer identifiers, for every table.

**Step 3.** Identify the foreign keys in the SalesOrderLine table. The SalesOrderLine table contains two foreign keys: SalesOrderID (referencing SalesOrder) and ItemID (referencing Item in the Master Data group). Trace each foreign key to the table it references and confirm that the referenced column is the primary key of that table. The ItemID foreign key is a cross-group bridge key because it connects the O2C group to the Master Data group, which is why its relationship line is drawn in amber.

**Step 4.** Read the cardinality and optionality of the relationship between Customer and SalesOrder. Find the line connecting the two tables. The Customer end shows two bars (exactly one), and the SalesOrder end shows a circle with a crow's foot (zero or many). Read the relationship aloud: "Each sales order belongs to exactly one customer. One customer can have zero or many sales orders." The circle tells you that a customer can exist in the database without having placed an order.

**Step 5.** Find the SalesOrderLine table. Notice that it sits between SalesOrder and Item. Trace its two foreign keys: SalesOrderID connects to the SalesOrder table, and ItemID connects to the Item table. At the SalesOrderLine end, the line from SalesOrder shows one or many (every order has at least one line), while the line from Item shows zero or many (some items have never been ordered). The SalesOrderLine table is the junction table that resolves the many-to-many relationship between sales orders and items.

**Step 6.** Trace the fulfillment path. From SalesOrderLine, follow the relationship to ShipmentLine (one order line can be shipped in zero, one, or several shipment lines). From ShipmentLine, follow the relationship to SalesInvoiceLine through the ShipmentLineID foreign key. Notice the symbols on this line: zero or one at both ends. Each shipment line is billed on at most one invoice line, and invoice lines for design services have no shipment line because nothing was shipped. From SalesInvoiceLine, move up to SalesInvoice (each invoice has one or many lines). From SalesInvoice, follow the settlement path to CashReceiptApplication and then to CashReceipt. One receipt can settle several invoices, and one invoice can be settled by several receipts, so CashReceiptApplication is a second junction table. You have now traced the full O2C path from order through fulfillment, billing, and settlement.

**Checkpoint.** You should now be able to answer the following questions by reading the O2C ER diagram. How many foreign keys does the SalesOrderLine table contain? (Two: SalesOrderID and ItemID.) Which tables serve as junction tables? (SalesOrderLine between SalesOrder and Item, and CashReceiptApplication between CashReceipt and SalesInvoice.) What is the cardinality of the relationship between Customer and SalesOrder? (One to zero or many: each order has exactly one customer, and a customer can have any number of orders, including none.) If you can answer all three questions correctly, you have the ER diagram reading skills you will need for the chapters ahead.
